persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Bora Özkent's day centered on the US midterms. Before the vote he said the market was pricing a Democratic win as dangerous for chips and AI infrastructure and that he disagreed; the **Nasdaq** had fallen 1.07% and the **SOX** semiconductor index 3.37% the day before, while new debt-raising by **Meta** and **Oracle** of about $20 billion each, the Marvell-Lumentum merger and the upcoming **Anthropic** IPO weighed on AI stocks. He still reads Anthropic's $17 billion Q3 revenue and the longer TrendForce lead times for memory, CPUs and ABF substrates as signs of strong demand; **Brent** fell from 116.72 to 104.77 on easing in Iran and the odds of a December rate hike eased from 85% to 73-76%.

Once results came in on the livestream, the market sold off hard and the Nasdaq 100 fell about 2%. In his view the real blow was the Texas and Ohio governor races rather than the Senate: governors in those data-center-heavy states can declare a moratorium. He sees no short-term impact beyond data centers, thinks the new Texas governor may be open to a compromise, but expects budget gridlock and a messy period. On the stream he also said he no longer calls **Intel** 'junk' but that management is still bad, and that **Nvidia** is 'definitely not a bubble'.

items.title: ABD Seçimleri Yapay Zekaya Karşı
items.summary: Ahead of the vote, betting markets and polls show Democrats well ahead; the market prices that as dangerous for chips and AI infrastructure, while Özkent disagrees. The Nasdaq fell 1.07% and the SOX 3.37% the previous day, with money rotating out of tech and energy into staples and financials. Marvell's stock-swap acquisition of Lumentum hit both shares hard; Meta and Oracle each seeking about $20 billion in new debt and equity and the upcoming Anthropic IPO ($1.5-1.6 trillion valuation, possibly absorbing $80-100 billion) are weighing on AI stocks. Per TrendForce, DRAM lead times are 19 weeks, CPUs 25-30 weeks and ABF 48-56 weeks, so products are as scarce as money, yet the market does not want to see it. Anthropic's Q3 revenue is $17 billion, compute costs grew faster than revenue and it has $895 billion of forward commitments; with $130 billion in cash Özkent finds the fear exaggerated. Brent fell from 116.72 to 104.77 on easing in Iran and the odds of a December rate hike dropped from 85% to 73-76%. Palantir (revenue $2.31 billion, up 96%) and Apple (EPS $2.05) beat expectations but the shares were sold. He thinks Republicans may keep the Senate 51-49 and Democrats will certainly take the House; his core view is unchanged and he is holding on AI infrastructure.

items.title: ABD Ara Seçimleri CANLI: Sonuçlar ve Piyasalar | Bora Özkent
items.summary: As results arrive on the livestream the market is selling hard, with the Nasdaq 100 down about 2%. Özkent says the real cause is the governor races rather than the Senate: Texas and Ohio are states where many data centers will be built, and a governor can declare a moratorium. Nobody had Democrats this far ahead in Texas in their numbers; he recalls Oracle declaring force majeure in Texas because it could not get power. He says nothing matters short-term except data centers and thinks the new Texas governor could compromise in return for jobs and local donations. If Democrats take both chambers he expects the budget to stall and things to get messy, though Trump is practical and may soften. He says the market did not expect a result this heavy against Republicans and that they trimmed positions yesterday. He retracts his earlier 'junk' call on Intel but says management is still poor and that, lacking memory, it is weak in both PCs and data centers. He adds that a solar company rose 9% yesterday and 3.5% today though its business model is troubled, and that Nvidia is definitely not a bubble.

assets.note: The Nasdaq 100 is down about 2%; the selling is driven by data center risk in Texas and Ohio.

persons.name: Heisenberg
persons.digest:
Heisenberg's day was about political risk after the US midterms: he calls Trump losing both the Senate and House a heavy defeat and does not see a Democratic win as positive for Turkey. He repeatedly explained that the real market risk lies in the 2027 budget, tax and trade-war process and that he expects no problem for 2026; he reminded readers that even with Republican majorities in both chambers the government stayed shut for about 1.5 months in 2026.

In the ongoing **Micron** debate from the day before, he defended his warning to those who bought options at $1,200, saying it holds despite the high IV and that, because of time and IV decay, some contracts would not profit even if the stock hit $2,000. He also wrote that similar penalties may hit other fund managers and that he no longer recommends TEFAS funds.

items.title: Democratic Congress win and the 2027 risk
items.summary: He called Trump losing both the Senate and the House a heavy defeat and wrote that his political room to maneuver will narrow sharply in the rest of his second term. He does not see a Democratic win as positive for Turkey, saying they have not helped it much in the past. For markets he sees possible periods of serious volatility in 2027 over the budget, tax policy, trade wars and political deadlock, but adds that uncertainty does not mean prices will fall outright.

items.title: Clarification on the 2027 budget risk
items.summary: He repeated that there is no problem for 2026 because the budget has passed and that the risk lies in the 2027 budget process. He recalled that the government stayed shut for about 1.5 months in 2026 even with Republican majorities in both chambers. He said markets dislike political uncertainty and budget crises and that volatility may rise.

items.title: Micron options and price discipline
items.summary: He defended his warning to those who bought $1,200 options: the price was already up 1,675% from the bottom of its range and buying options at 98% IV was not rational. He said he had written that better prices for spot buyers could appear at support zones and that one user bought the same company 40% cheaper. He argued a great company is not a good investment at every price and that, because of time and IV decay, some contracts would not profit even if the stock reached $2,000.

assets.note: Options bought at $1,200 are not profiting because of time and IV decay; the stock is still more than 1,200% above its range bottom. (The company in the previous day's post is Micron.)

items.title: TEFAS fund manager penalties
items.summary: He wrote that other fund managers are likely to receive the same penalties in the near term. Although he was among the first to explain TEFAS funds, he no longer recommends them to anyone and says investors must educate themselves.

assets.note: New contract data is weak despite revenue growth; the stock fell 9%.

items.title: Meta sells $15 billion bond
items.summary: Meta priced its $15 billion bond sale, paying up to 7.5% on 30-year debt (5-year 5.85%, 7-year 6.25%, 10-year 6.55%, 20-year 7.35%). The offering drew about $58 billion in orders, nearly 4x the amount sold.

assets.note: Orders were 4x the $15 billion bond, but borrowing costs are rising.

items.title: Chinese firms' Nvidia RTX order
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese AI firms ordered 6 million RTX Pro 5500 chips worth about $70 billion but expect only about 1% in four months, several thousand chips by year-end.

assets.note: Chinese clients will receive only 1% of the $70 billion order.

items.title: Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Per the WSJ, Iran is escalating attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz using underwater drones and limpet mines. Preliminary Kpler data show oil flows averaged 7.8 million bpd last week, just 45% of the prewar level.

items.title: Novo Nordisk Q3 earnings
items.summary: Sales DKK 79.195 billion (est. 73.83 billion), up 6% YoY; EPS DKK 3.79 missed estimates (5.09) and is down 16% YoY, operating profit DKK 23.011 billion (est. 27.89 billion). It raised FY26 guidance; Wegovy pill prescriptions reached 3.6 million in Q3.

assets.note: Sales beat, EPS and operating profit missed.

items.title: Citi: memory undersupply persists in 2027
items.summary: Citi still expects memory undersupply in 2027: DRAM demand is expected to grow 28% vs 24% supply, narrowing the deficit to 3.8% from 8.7%; NAND demand is projected to grow 26% vs 22% supply.

items.title: S&P 500 historically after midterms
items.summary: Kalshi gives Democrats a 93% chance of the House and 74% of the Senate. The S&P 500 finished higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950 (average gain 15.4%). In 1986, 1990 and 2006, when Democrats took Congress under a Republican president, it averaged -0.5% the next day, +3.4% after 1 month and +10.9% after 1 year.

assets.note: Higher 12 months after every midterm since 1950, averaging 15.4%.
